 Four-year-old latest dengue fatality in Iloilo
 By Rjay Zuriaga Castor
 November 16, 2026
 70
 Resize 
 Small 
 Medium 
 Large 
 ILOILO CITY — A four-year-old boy from the City Proper district became the latest dengue fatality after seeking medical attention only after several days of fever and other symptoms, prompting health officials to reiterate the importance of early consultation and testing.
 The child, who succumbed to complications of dengue on Oct. 29, initially developed a fever on Oct. 26 but was treated at home with home remedies, according to Dr. Roland Jay Fortuna, assistant city health officer (CHO).
 Although the fever temporarily subsided, it returned the following day, accompanied by vomiting.
 Instead of immediately seeking medical attention, the family initially resorted to traditional massage treatment and gave the child paracetamol.
 By Oct. 28, the boy had developed poor appetite, abdominal pain, and lethargy. He was brought to a health center only the following day and subsequently referred to a hospital.

 Fortuna described the incident as another case of late consultation, stressing that dengue testing is already available at city health centers even on the first day of fever.
 “Another case of late consultation. Now the test kits we use are the dengue duo, where even on day one of fever we can already catch if the patient is positive for dengue and we can already focus on the monitoring,” Fortuna said in an interview on Nov. 10.
 Advertisement 
 “We appeal that if there is fever, go to the health centers,” he added.
 Fortuna explained that a dengue duo test detects dengue virus markers during the acute phase of infection, typically within the first seven days of symptoms, with results available in 15 to 20 minutes.
 The CHO official also emphasized that residents should seek consultation even for low-grade fever, particularly when body temperature reaches 37.8 degrees Celsius.
 He stressed that dengue testing at city health centers is free, and patients who initially test negative on the first day of fever may also undergo repeat testing on the second or third day if symptoms persist.
 Advertisement 
 “Early detection, early monitoring. If we need to hydrate patients, we have oral hydration in our health centers,” Fortuna said.
 As of Nov. 7, Iloilo City had recorded 844 dengue cases, up 46.8 percent from the 575 cases reported during the same period last year.
 The city also logged nine deaths, three times the three fatalities recorded in the corresponding period in 2025.
 No outbreak yet
 Advertisement 
 While the city’s dengue cases have exceeded alert and epidemic thresholds, he said the CHO considers other epidemiological indicators before declaring an outbreak.
 These include comparisons with the average number of cases over the previous three to five years, as well as the city’s attack rate and case fatality rate.
 Fortuna said the 844 cases recorded so far remain below the 2021-2025 average of 1,004 cases, although the current tally is higher than the corresponding figures in some previous years.
 The city’s attack rate stood at 182.66, also below the five-year average of 190.74, according to Fortuna.
 Advertisement 
 He added that Iloilo City currently has the second-lowest attack rate compared with other provinces.
 Meanwhile, the city’s case fatality rate has risen to 1.07 percent.
